lead: since the afternoon you said the words out loud you have ended a city, a working life, and the person who did both — and the woman across the table stayed married to each one in turn.
sun: every few years the interior goes completely. the plans you made at the start, the people you had round, the man she actually chose: finished inside a season, no gradient on offer, nothing kept warm. the walls do not move. she wakes into the same terms with somebody new performing them, and they get performed exactly, because what is owed has never once come off with the weather.
moon: nothing in you knows how to leave a thing like this. the equipment that finishes a city in a fortnight does not scale down to a bond entered on purpose, and there is no slow exit in you either. so it gets held the way it was taken: by decision, renewed across a hundred unremarkable evenings nobody watching would call devotion.
pull: she has been married to three different men and can date the arrival of each. all three said the same words, and the one keeping them now never heard them said.
tension: twenty years of it gets offered as proof that nothing was ever wrong with you, by somebody who watched two of the endings from a distance. it does the opposite work: if you can hold that, the departures cannot have been weather, and get read as choices made against people. the bond becomes evidence about your character, argued by people who attended none of them, and the woman who sat through all three is quoted by both sides.
cost: the marriage has never had a year of somebody half-present in it, and never will: a bad season here finishes like every other season, whole, and the following one starts clean rather than curdling for a decade. what she is holding is the terms. the man who wanted her went out in one of the turns, and nobody, including you, can put a date on which.

lead: you have not gone up with them in five years and are not going to. your number on the roll is still the lowest one alive — a roll runs on dates, and a date cannot turn.
sun: the stopping was done the way you do everything: inside a week, with the kit handed in on the friday. the position could not be handed in. an ending has to be given to somebody with the standing to take it, and there has never been anybody at that height here, so yours went downward instead — to people who had no option of refusing it, and who have gone on ringing you since.
moon: the same thing sets up wherever you land: within a year of arriving you are the one being asked, with no application and no appointment. nobody grants it and nobody can take it away. so each life you have finished has left a set of people standing below the line you held, and every one of those sets is still owed the answer nobody else in it can supply.
pull: there is nobody above you to end it with, so you ended it downward, and the people you ended it to still ring at night with the thing nobody else can be asked.
tension: the calls did not stop when you did, so on paper you kept everyone. all of it is addressed to the position. nobody has rung in twenty years about anything that did not need somebody senior on it, and from the outside that reads as a person who left and is still wanted by the crew they left. what is actually standing is a line of people with a question and nobody else at that height to put it to.
cost: you can finish a thing on a tuesday and have it finished, because the permission is your own. the judging runs the same way: every break you have made was reviewed by the one who made it, and the people it landed on were below the line, where disagreement comes out as a question rather than an objection. so it goes into the record as sound and stays there.

lead: the place you two ran closed for the reason everybody agreed on. three years after you had finished with the whole of it you got under that reason, and the one beneath it has his name on it.
sun: nothing gets examined while you are still standing in it. the season closes first, the whole of it is over to the skin, and only then does the floor come up. so the instrument works only on what is already dead, and every true cause you have found has arrived about a life with nobody left in it to inform.
moon: the digging did not stop where it would have been enough. three explanations were on offer — the trade changed, the money got thin, two men grew apart — and you went under all three. nothing in you calls the search off where an answer would do. a foundation cannot be looked at without lifting the thing standing on it, and by then there was nothing standing.
pull: you went to the bottom and his name was under there. he still rings twice a year. you still turn up, and pay what is owed, and he has never once been told.
tension: people who watched you walk out of it in a fortnight also watched you spend three years going through what was left, and they read the two together as somebody who never got over it. the leaving was as complete as leavings get. what continued was the excavation, which needs no participant and no feeling. the difference is invisible from any distance: what anybody sees is a person still on the site years later, moving material by hand.
cost: you have the real reason each of your lives ended, in order, with the evidence for all of it. none of it has ever altered a payment. what he is owed was set before you knew, and knowing has not moved it by a pound or an hour, so the finding stays at the depth it was made and the tie above it runs untouched.

lead: you stopped believing over one winter, completely, in the way that leaves nothing lapsed — and you were at the door on sunday, counting them in, as you have been every week since.
sun: it went the way weather goes: at full strength on the second sunday of the month and absent by the fourth, with no residue — no fond version kept for funerals, no half of it retained for the singing. nothing of the belief is in you. the office is. you hold the roll, the keys and the sick list, and the holding never flickered in the season the rest of it went.
moon: the believing years had you at the edge of the room the whole time — arriving early, staying late, knowing every name, and standing where a person can leave without the singing stopping. and you can tell within a season which of them are holding the place up and which are passing through on a bad year. it has never once been your congregation to sort.
pull: the belief went in a season and you have not missed a sunday since. the most reliable person in that building has not believed a word of it in six years, and holds the keys.
tension: the place has machinery for doubt — a phase gets prayed over, a rota gets arranged — and nothing at all for a thing that is finished. the week you said it plainly you were handed a season of gentle attention and a study group. the ones who left years ago read your attendance as somebody who could not go through with it. both readings describe a person on the way somewhere, which is the one thing you are not.
cost: the roll is accurate, the visits happen, and whoever needs somebody at the hospital at night gets one, more reliably than in the believing years. there is no date on it. the tie was made to people rather than the thing they meet for, so it runs as long as they do, and you will be at that door for the funerals of everyone who prayed over you.
